stories.title: Nonlinear hydrological responses to intermediate development pathways in semi-arid watersheds
stories.description: Hydrological vulnerability in semi-arid watersheds is increasingly shaped by coupled climate and land-use change, yet the relative importance of runoff and sediment dynamics remains unclear. Here, we develop an integrated socio-hydrological framework that combines SWAT modeling, CA–Markov land-use projections, and CMIP6-based Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) to quantify runoff, sediment yield, and vulnerability at the sub-watershed scale. Across 16 sub-watersheds and two future periods (2021–2040; 2041–2052), simulations reveal pronounced spatial heterogeneity in runoff responses, whereas Sediment yield increased by approximately 15–30% relative to the baseline period under all evaluated scenarios. This divergence indicates a systematic decoupling of runoff and sediment dynamics, with sediment emerging as a more sensitive indicator of watershed degradation. Notably, the intermediate SSP2-4.5 pathway produces more consistent hydrological responses across sub-watersheds than SSP5-8.5, highlighting nonlinear relationships between development trajectories and hydrological risk. A spatially explicit Integrated Vulnerability Index incorporating dynamic adaptive capacity identifies persistent vulnerability hotspots in central and downstream sub-watersheds. These findings demonstrate that moderate development pathways can induce disproportionate hydrological stress and underscore the importance of sediment-focused, transferable frameworks for climate adaptation in semi-arid regions.

stories.title: Complex LED light regimens differentially regulate tomato growth, yield formation and fruit quality
stories.description: Tomato is a very important horticultural crop worldwide, valued for its economic significance and nutritional benefits. Tomato fruits are rich in essential nutrients and bioactive compounds, including vitamins, carotenoids, and polyphenols. In this study, we investigated how light quality and intensity influence plant growth, yield, and fruit quality parameters in tomato. Plants were grown under six different light regimens, including varying red-to-blue ratios, wide spectral white light with or without far-red application at two light intensities (300 μmol m−2 s−1 and 500 μmol m−2 s−1). Our results demonstrated that blue light promoted flowering and fruit set, leading to a higher number of fruits; however, under lower light intensity, this resulted in smaller fruits. In contrast, red-dominant or broad-spectrum light conditions produced less but larger and sweeter fruits, even at low light intensity. Higher light intensity overall increased total yield and sugar accumulation, also indicating enhanced photosynthetic activity and preferential allocation of assimilates to fruit biomass. Interestingly, lycopene content was not affected by any light treatment at all. Our findings showed that a careful consideration is required when selecting the intensity and spectral composition of an artificial lighting in indoor cultivation systems.

stories.title: An efficient photo-Favorskii rearrangement of α-chloroketones for the synthesis of 2-arylpropionic acids
stories.description: 2-Arylpropionic acids, exemplified by ibuprofen, are important structural motifs widely found in bioactive molecules and pharmaceutical agents, and their industrial synthesis is therefore of considerable significance. Herein, we report a systematic study of the photo-Favorskii rearrangement synthesis of 2-arylpropionic acids using zinc acetate as a cost-effective, readily available, and environmentally benign acid scavenger. Under mild visible-light irradiation conditions, this protocol enables efficient conversion of α-chloroketones into the corresponding 2-arylpropionic acids, delivering moderate to good yields across a broad range of more than 11 substrates. This work demonstrates the potential of zinc acetate for sustainable organic synthesis and provides an environmentally benign, efficient strategy for the preparation of valuable carboxylic acid derivatives.

stories.title: Disentangling neural and physiological contributions to fNIRS signals during active and passive auditory tasks
stories.description: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) is increasingly used to study speech processing because it balances spatial and temporal resolution, but fNIRS signals are susceptible to physiological interference, particularly during active-response tasks. This study examined how systemic-physiological signals influence task-evoked activation in an active word-monitoring task compared to a passive-listening paradigm. Three noise-correction models were applied: No-Correction, Short-Channel (SC) Correction addressing extra-cerebral signals, and combined Short-Channel + Physiology (SC + Physiology) Correction that also accounted for systemic physiology. Active-response trials showed negative amplitudes in the No-Correction model, consistent with scalp hemodynamic suppression. SC Correction shifted amplitudes to positive values and eliminated task differences in dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, secondary auditory cortex, and motor regions, suggesting that these task differences were at least partly attributable to superficial physiology. After adding systemic-physiology correction, the active-vs-passive difference in primary auditory cortex was no longer significant, however, the direct comparison between the SC Correction and SC + Physiology models did not reach significance. These findings indicate that active-response fNIRS paradigms are vulnerable to physiological interference and that global-mean-based short-channel correction substantially attenuates this interference and appears to reveal task-evoked activity that the uncorrected signal obscures.
